summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -7 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates 0; dollar −; brl −; mxn −; risk −; energy −; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Rough rice +4.6%; weakest: Lean hogs -15.3%. Key releases ahead: US Core PCE Price Index m/m (11-25 8:30 AM ET); US Prelim GDP q/q (11-25 8:30 AM ET).

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 4.92% (-8 bp in a month), 2-year 4.63% (-6 bp); 2s10s curve +29 bp (-2 bp in a month). Yields are little changed on the month. T-bill yield 4.15% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 103.94 (+2.1% in a month, +5.8% YTD). A stronger dollar makes US grain, oilseeds, cotton and meat dearer abroad. USD/BRL 5.939 (+17.6% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.651 (-0.4%); USD/MXN 19.31 (+3.1%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -5.1% in a month (+5.7% YTD); VIX 28.3. Risk-off: funds tend to cut commodity length along with equities.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 80.31 $/bbl (-20.4% in a month), Brent 87.07, ULSD 3.666 $/gal (-21.6%), natural gas 3.58 (+2.1%). Lower crude weighs on soybean oil and corn through biofuel margins and on cotton via cheaper polyester.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -16.4% in a month, Shanghai Composite -3.9%, Hang Seng -3.8%, yuan +0.4% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 8 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (24%); S&P GSCI -15.4% in a month; gold -9.3%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.

events_ahead.title: Core PCE Price Index m/m
